questions.prompt: In astronomical image processing, what does the FITS file format stand for?
questions.note: FITS is the standard data format used widely in astronomy.

questions.prompt: What specific technique is most commonly used in software to help users visually identify moving objects (like asteroids) against a background of fixed stars?
options: Image Blinking (rapidly switching between sequential images)
questions.note: Blinking sequential images makes moving objects jump out against fixed stars.

questions.prompt: Right Ascension (RA) in the equatorial coordinate system is the astronomical equivalent of Earth's:
questions.note: Right Ascension is analogous to longitude on the sky sphere.

questions.prompt: Declination (Dec) in the equatorial coordinate system is the astronomical equivalent of Earth's:
questions.note: Declination is analogous to latitude and measures north/south angle.

questions.prompt: Astronomers classify asteroids into three main compositional types. Which of the following represents the most common type, composed largely of carbonaceous materials?
questions.note: C-type asteroids are carbon-rich and are the most common class.

questions.prompt: "Trojan" asteroids in our solar system are primarily known for sharing an orbit with which major planet?
questions.note: The best-known Trojan populations share Jupiter's orbit near Lagrange points.

options: The plane of Earth's orbit around the Sun.
The shadow cast by Earth on the Moon.
The alignment of all planets in a straight line.
The boundary of the solar system.
questions.note: The ecliptic is the orbital plane of Earth around the Sun.

questions.prompt: Which theoretical, spherical region at the outermost edge of our solar system is believed to be the source of most long-period comets?
questions.note: The Oort Cloud is thought to supply many long-period comets.

questions.prompt: Which parameter of a telescope determines its "light-gathering power," allowing it to see fainter objects?
questions.note: Larger aperture captures more light and improves faint-object visibility.

questions.prompt: What is the expected final evolutionary state of a medium-mass star like our Sun?
questions.note: After shedding outer layers, Sun-like stars end as white dwarfs.

questions.prompt: Based on its structure, the Milky Way is classified as what type of galaxy?
questions.note: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy.

questions.prompt: Which space telescope, launched in 1990, is renowned for its deep field images revealing thousands of galaxies?
questions.note: Hubble's deep field observations transformed our view of the distant universe.

questions.prompt: In astronomy, the "habitable zone" (or Goldilocks Zone) around a star is defined as the region where:
options: Radiation levels are safe for humans
Liquid water can exist on a planet's surface
questions.note: The habitable zone is where temperatures may allow stable liquid water.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the effect where light from a receding astronomical object is shifted to longer wavelengths?
questions.note: Receding objects show redshift as their light stretches to longer wavelengths.

questions.prompt: If an asteroid is described as having a highly "eccentric" orbit, what does that mean about its orbital path?
options: It orbits in the opposite direction of the planets
Its orbit is highly elongated or oval-shaped
It frequently changes its orbital plane
questions.note: High eccentricity means the orbit is far from circular.
